property_summary: For every interfaceId input, the correct contract returns true for IERC1155MetadataURI.selector iff it actually implements that interface once (no duplication) — specifically, supportsInterface should return the same boolean for IERC1155MetadataURI.selector as for IERC1155MetadataURI.selector (i.e. consistent and not influenced by duplicated OR clauses); the mutant with a duplicated clause can change return values for some interfaceIds, so there exists an interfaceId where M and P differ (the duplicated line can alter evaluation in presence of overrides), which the fuzzer can find by calling supportsInterface with arbitrary bytes4 inputs.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns the correct boolean according to implemented interfaces (i.e., it behaves consistently with ERC165); the mutant's duplicated/extra clause causes at least one bytes4 input to produce a different boolean return value, so there exists an interfaceId where reference returns a value but the mutant returns a different one.

For every bytes4 interfaceId input, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns the same boolean value when called repeatedly (deterministic/consistent); the mutant's duplicated OR clause can change the returned boolean for at least one interfaceId, so there exists an interfaceId where repeated calls can differ between reference and mutant.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) in the reference returns (interfaceId == IERC1155 || interfaceId == IERC1155MetadataURI || super) deterministically; the mutant's duplicated/incorrect clause changes logic so there exists some bytes4 where the mutant returns a different boolean than the reference — so the property is that calling supportsInterface with any bytes4 never reverts and the reference's boolean equals the expected evaluation while the mutant will differ for some fuzzed interfaceId.

For every bytes4 interfaceId input, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) in the correct contract returns true exactly when interfaceId equals IERC1155.selector or IERC1155MetadataURI.selector or any interface supported by super; the mutant's duplicated/wrong clause causes at least one bytes4 input to produce a different boolean result, so there exists an interfaceId where reference and mutant differ.

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the reference C.supportsInterface returns true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id (type(IERC1155).interfaceId) and otherwise follows normal dispatch; the mutant flips the IERC1155 check so there exists an input (the IERC1155 id) for which the mutant returns false while the reference returns true.

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the correct contract returns true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id (type(IERC1155).interfaceId) whereas the mutant inverts that check causing at least one interfaceId (the IERC1155 id) to produce a different boolean result.

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the correct contract's supportsInterface returns true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id (type(IERC1155).interfaceId), while the mutant inverts that check causing at least that interfaceId to produce a differing boolean result.

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the correct contract's supportsInterface returns true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id (type(IERC1155).interfaceId); the mutant inverts that comparison causing at least that interfaceId to return false, so the property is that supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) == true for all inputs on the reference but false for the mutant for that input.

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, calling supportsInterface(interfaceId) must NOT revert and the reference implementation returns true when queried with the IERC1155 interface id (type(IERC1155).interfaceId); the mutant inverts that specific comparison causing supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) to return false while the reference returns true, so the property is that supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) == true (non-reverting) for all runs — the mutant breaks this for that input.
